title: Echosphere Pharma — Private VPC / Networking Discovery
summary: Intro discovery to understand Echosphere's private VPC requirements for a Redwood Private deployment. Covered networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region restrictions, egress and latency concerns, KMS integration and audit logs, and next steps for a PoC including network diagram and checklist.
next_steps: Redwood: share private deployment networking runbook and example VPC templates (Jordan) by 2027-03-12
Customer: circulate internal network diagram and preferred region list (Anita) by 2027-03-15
Schedule SE-led deep dive and pilot scoping session w/ infra (Priya + Anita) week of 2027-03-22
action_items: Jordan: send networking runbook + SOC2 and architecture deck — due 2027-03-12
Anita: share VPC CIDR ranges and peering constraints — due 2027-03-15
Priya: prepare initial pilot config (instance counts, expected TPS) — due 2027-03-18
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Kim: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we have Priya our SE, Liam's on in case we need ops details. how's everybody doing?
00:08 Michael Chen: doing well thanks. we have a few people on our side — Anita who owns cloud, Roberto for security, and Sara PMing the initiative.

00:15 Jordan Kim: great quick agenda: understand current infra, what you need from a private deployment, network constraints (peering, endpoints), security requirements like kms and audit logs, and next steps. sound good?

00:25 Anita Patel: yep that works. high level we want to run Redwood Private in our VPC — can't send data over public internet, we need private connectivity. also region constraints — some workloads must stay in eu-west-1, others us-east-1.
00:40 Priya Rao: thanks Anita. quick clarifying q: do you prefer VPC peering or aws privatelink/private endpoints, or are you open to either?

00:48 Anita Patel: we're evaluating. peering is simpler for us but we have overlapping CIDRs in some accounts, so peering might not be possible for all environments. privatelink sounds good but we need egress cost estimates and any added latency info.

00:59 Roberto Diaz: from security perspective we need full audit logs, we use KMS for encryption and we'd like support for customer-managed keys (HSM integration possibly later). also SSO via SAML and RBAC mapping to our idp.

01:12 Priya Rao: good notes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS keys and we can integrate with HSM providers — that's a common ask. we also produce audit logs and can push to your cloud logging (we typically write to CloudWatch / Splunk via VPC endpoints or syslog).
01:28 Michael Chen: how does networking look operationally? if we do privatelink endpoints, do we need to open specific subnets? And what about internal DNS resolution to the endpoints?

01:40 Priya Rao: for AWS PrivateLink we surface network interfaces in your VPC — you create interface endpoints in the subnets you want accessibility from. DNS-wise, we can provide a private DNS name that resolves to the endpoint, or you can use your own Route53 entries. we'll include a template.

01:55 Liam Torres: adding — for Dedicated vs Private there's difference: Hosted path uses public endpoints with mTLS, Dedicated is reserved infra in our cloud with some network controls, and Private gives you a control plane or data plane inside your VPC depending on the mode. we should map exact traffic flows in a diagram, we'll share our reference diagrams.

02:12 Anita Patel: ok that helps. for egress costs — if flow goes from our VPC to Redwood's service endpoints in the same region via privatelink, do we still pay standard interface endpoint charges? And is there any cross-region data movement we should watch for?

02:25 Priya Rao: yes there are interface endpoint charges and standard data processing fees for privatelink; we will include an example cost calc. Cross-region traffic is the bigger concern — if the serving plane is in a different region than the VPC you'll incur cross-region egress. we can pin model replicas to regions to avoid cross-region egress for sensitive workloads.
02:43 Roberto Diaz: when you say pin replicas do you mean we can demand eu-only compute for eu workloads? we need contractual guarantees about data residency for PHI and regulatory workloads.

02:55 Jordan Kim: yes, in Redwood Private you can specify region constraints and node placement. For contractual commitments we offer private deployments and can lock region placement as part of the enterprise agreement. we'll share the SOC2/ISO and data residency language in the contract addendum.
03:10 Michael Chen: great. can you talk about peering constraints? we have a hub/spoke model and some spokes have overlapping ranges with third parties, which makes peering tricky.

03:22 Priya Rao: overlapping CIDR is a common blocker for classic VPC peering. In those cases customers use PrivateLink (interface endpoints) or set up transit gateway with NAT/translations. Another option is to host a shared VPC that Redwood connects to — depends on your networking policies. we'll outline the pros/cons in the runbook.
03:38 Anita Patel: Transit gateway is attractive but we have policy limits on cross-account TGWs. would Redwood support TGW attachments?

03:45 Liam Torres: yes we can work with TGW attachments; operationally we need to coordinate routing tables and prefix lists. we normally publish a small set of allowed prefixes for the service and accept route entries. we'll need a peering/tgw handshake step in the runbook.
04:00 Roberto Diaz: what about private endpoints for the control plane vs data plane? we want control signals to go out but data must stay within our VPC with no internet egress.

04:10 Priya Rao: we support a model where the control plane can be in our managed control plane (optionally private connectivity over VPN or peering) while the data plane runs in your VPC — that ensures no data egress. for some customers we provide a fully air-gapped package as well.
04:28 Michael Chen: any limitations on model sizes / GPU types in private deployments? we plan to run LLM inference that needs KV cache persistence and quantized models.

04:38 Liam Torres: hardware options are flexible but some specialized kernels require certain GPU families; we'll capture recommended instance types in the pilot config. KV cache is supported and we can bind cache storage to local NVMe or networked volumes depending on perf needs. quantization is supported in our runtime but we'll do perf validation during the PoC.
04:55 Anita Patel: perf validation — can we run a benchmark in our VPC with sample traffic? we want latency P50/P95 numbers and token throughput.

05:03 Priya Rao: absolutely. typical approach: we spin up a pilot cluster in your preferred region, run a controlled load test with your prompt set, collect latency and throughput, and then iterate on batching and caching configs. we'll provide the harness and a spreadsheet for results.
05:18 Roberto Diaz: security — how do you handle KMS keys? do you have access to our CMKs?

05:24 Priya Rao: no, we do not require key material. we integrate with your KMS and use encryption-in-place; you control the CMK and can rotate keys. For HSM-backed keys we have options to integrate via customer-managed HSM or cloud HSM providers; we'll document the flow.
05:36 Michael Chen: audit logs — format and retention? we need export to our SIEM with immutable logs for compliance.

05:42 Jordan Kim: we can stream detailed audit logs (request/response metadata, model version, user ID, route) to your logging endpoint. retention is configurable; for compliance-grade retention we can push to your S3 with object lock or to an external SIEM. we'll include sample log schema.

05:58 Anita Patel: one question on DNS: some teams manage DNS centrally and won't permit private DNS records for interface endpoints. if that's the case, we need IPs or a static naming scheme. does Redwood support static IPs for endpoints?

06:10 Liam Torres: interface endpoints use ENIs so IPs are assigned by your subnet, but they can change on re-creation. For static addressing we recommend placing endpoints in subnets with reserved secondary IPs or using NLB fronting where we can give static IPs. we'll document options and caveats.
06:26 Sara Lo: timeline — we want to pilot in two regions in Q2. is that feasible?

06:31 Jordan Kim: yes Q2 pilot is reasonable. steps: share networking runbook, you provide diagrams and CIDRs, we'll propose pilot infra and cost estimate, then run perf tests. target kickoff by 2027-03-22 for SE deep dive and infra planning.
06:43 Anita Patel: can you send a sample VPC template and any Terraform modules? that will speed internal reviews.

06:48 Priya Rao: yes we'll share TF modules and CloudFormation examples in the runbook link. link: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-vpc-runbook (note: placeholder) — contains templates, route examples, and security checklist.
06:59 Michael Chen: perfect. any gotchas you commonly see?

07:03 Priya Rao: two common ones: overlapping CIDRs and missing route permissions for peering/tgw; and second is tokenization differences causing higher-than-expected token counts — we recommend test prompts to estimate cost. Also watch out for cross-account IAM permissions for interface endpoint acceptance.
07:17 Roberto Diaz: what about penetration testing and third-party audits? we have an internal pentest schedule and need to include Redwood components in scope.
07:25 Jordan Kim: we can coordinate and provide a contact for security assessments. we publish our security docs and will work through a PoA for pentesting. SOC2/ISO reports we can share under NDA.
07:36 Anita Patel: ok great. will you include network diagrams that show control plane traffic vs data plane and expected ports?
07:42 Priya Rao: yes, the runbook has a standard diagram and we'll annotate ports (TLS 443, KV cache ports, internal health checks) and recommended subnet setup.
07:54 Michael Chen: curious about model version pinning — if we pin to a specific model in region, how does rollouts work? we can't accept surprise quality regressions.

08:02 Liam Torres: you can pin model versions per route. rollouts are handled via canary policies; we support traffic split for canary and automatic rollback on defined quality metrics. we'll work with your eval set to define regression thresholds during the PoC.
08:18 Sara Lo: ok next steps recap?

08:21 Jordan Kim: recap: 1) Jordan sends runbook + SOC2 docs by 03/12. 2) Anita shares VPC diagrams and CIDR ranges by 03/15. 3) Priya prepares pilot config and cost estimate by 03/18. 4) schedule deep-dive week of 03/22. anyone disagree?
08:35 Anita Patel: all good on our side.
08:38 Michael Chen: yep thanks everyone, looking forward to the runbook.
08:42 Roberto Diaz: one last note — we may request HSM integration details earlier; please include an HSM appendix if possible.
08:49 Priya Rao: noted, we'll add HSM appendix and sample network ACLs. thanks folks!
08:53 Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the SE deep dive. bye.
45:00 (meeting end)
